overall: Atlanta is experiencing a remarkably suppressed morning warm-up, with temperatures essentially flat at 73.4°F since midnight due to persistent 100% overcast skies and an extremely low ceiling of ~400 ft (122m). The dewpoint of ~70°F indicates very high humidity, and the 30-minute velocity has dropped to 0.0°F/hr, suggesting warming has stalled despite the clock ticking toward the expected mid-afternoon peak around 14:00–15:00 ET.
forecast_obs_notes: The NWP models span a range of 83.4°F (HRRR) to 86.4°F (NBM), well below the NWS text forecast of ~88°F — and the HRRR, which best captures current cloud structure, is the most pessimistic. The META (fused) model places peak probability at 84–85°F (29.4%), with the intraday model converging near 86–87°F if clouds break. The persistent heavy overcast this morning is tracking significantly cooler than the NWS narrative implies, making 88°F appear overly optimistic.
max_temp_prediction: With only ~4 hours of potential heating remaining before the predicted 14:00–15:00 ET peak, and the current temperature stuck at 73.4°F under full overcast with a ceiling below 400 ft, reaching 88°F would require an implausible ~3.7°F/hr sustained warming rate. A partial cloud break could allow a run to the mid-80s, but given the stalled warming trend, negative acceleration, and HRRR signal at 83.4°F, the most likely outcome is a high in the 84–86°F range. Confidence is moderate — the wildcard is how quickly (or whether) the overcast breaks ahead of the afternoon peak.
